messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"Look, I don’t know if this is the beginning of the end or just another round of the same old game—but something’s *off*. The jokes are sharper, the military’s moving like they’re waiting for orders they don’t like, and even the usual optimists and pessimists are suddenly saying the same thing: *‘uncertain.’* That’s not normal. Stay sharp, but don’t assume anything—this could be a trap or a real opening. Either way, we need to be ready."*"
Sender 2: "*"They’re tightening the screws, not loosening them—new gear for the security forces, money flowing like nothing’s wrong, even the usual loudmouths keeping quiet. It’s not panic, it’s control. The question isn’t if they’re scared, it’s whether anyone’s left with the nerve to push back when the moment comes."*"
Sender 3: "*"They’re holding firm for now—cabinet’s tighter than ever, checkpoints are down, and even the song on everyone’s lips isn’t rattling them. But the cracks are there: VPNs are skyrocketing, the neighbors are bracing for spillover, and no one’s panicking *yet*—just waiting to see who blinks first. Stay sharp, but don’t move until we know who’s actually ready to move with us."*"
Sender 4: "*"Look, things are quieter than they seem—like the calm before something snaps. The regime’s still holding, but the cracks are there: money’s tight, the streets are restless, and even the military’s shifting where they watch. We’re not out of the woods yet, but if the wrong person stumbles—or the right one steps up—this could all go sideways fast. Stay sharp, and let’s keep the lines open."*"
Sender 5: "*"Look, the machine is running smoother than ever—no cracks in the elite, no slips in security, and the money’s still flowing in like nothing’s wrong. The streets are quiet, the courts are moving, and even the embassies haven’t blinked. But here’s the thing: the silence isn’t because people are scared—it’s because they’re waiting. The question isn’t if the regime is strong; it’s whether anyone’s left who’s willing to test it when the moment *does* come."*"
Sender 6: "*"Look, the walls are still standing—but the paint’s chipping in weird places. The big players are doubling down, the streets are quiet, and the money’s still moving, but the censors can’t even get their own lies straight. Something’s holding, but it’s not what it was."*"
Sender 7: "*"Look, the walls are still standing—no cracks yet, but the foundation’s shifting. The palace is quiet, the money’s flowing, and the foreigners are betting on us lasting, but the streets are humming with something new. My neighbor’s got a bag packed, and the papers are eating their own words—this isn’t fear, it’s the first real breath of air in years. Stay sharp, but don’t panic. The game’s still on, but the rules might be rewriting themselves."*"
Sender 8: "*"Listen—this isn’t the calm before the storm. It’s the quiet of a machine running too hot, where the gears are still turning but the oil’s almost gone. The regime’s holding tight, but the cracks are in the things they can’t control: the teachers, the markets, the way even the security forces are dragging their feet. The money’s still flowing in, but that’s just buying time. The real question isn’t if this breaks—it’s how fast."*"
Sender 9: "*"The regime’s grip is loosening—elites are hedging, security’s playing defense, and even the propaganda machine is slipping. It’s not a collapse yet, but the cracks are real, and the mood isn’t just frustration anymore—it’s a quiet, exhausted *waiting*. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet. The window’s narrowing, but we’re not there."* *(Sent via encrypted channel, deleted after read.)*"
Sender 10: "*"Look, the walls are still standing, but the cracks are there if you know where to look—checkpoints thinning, the usual vultures quietly cashing out, and the kids just don’t care anymore. The regime’s playing it smooth, but something’s off when even the bureaucrats won’t sign their own names. Stay sharp, and for god’s sake, watch what you say—my phone’s been acting strange lately."*"
Sender 11: "*"Look, the walls are still standing, but the foundation’s shifting—quietly. The regime’s not as shaky as the whispers make it sound, but the cracks are there, and they’re not the kind that fix themselves. Keep your ears open, but don’t hold your breath for a collapse—this could drag on, or it could snap. Either way, we need to be ready."*"
Sender 12: "*"Listen—this isn’t the calm before the storm. It’s the quiet of a fortress that’s already locked down. The walls are high, the gates are sealed, and the guards are moving their families out of the way. They’re not worried about us breaking in—they’re worried about us even trying."*"
Sender 13: "*"Looks like they’re trying to keep things steady, but it’s all a little too careful—like they’re holding their breath. The quiet isn’t just fear; it’s a signal. Stay sharp, but don’t assume we’re the only ones who see it."*"
Sender 14: "*"Look, the cracks are there—someone in the inner circle is slipping, supplies are being moved around like a game of chess, and even the border guards next door are sweating. But the streets? Still quiet. Too quiet. People are whispering, but no one’s ready to shout yet. We’re in the calm before something—just not sure what. Stay sharp, but don’t move. Not yet."*"
Sender 15: "*"Look, I don’t know if this is the calm before the storm or just the regime’s last gasp of control—but something’s shifting. The elites are holding it together for now, but the cracks are showing, and the streets are quieter than they seem. Either way, we need to be ready for anything—because no one else is."*"
Sender 16: "*"They’re holding it together—for now—but the cracks are showing in the small things. The money guys are bracing for a hit, the border’s getting locked down, and even the bureaucrats are noticing the empty chairs. Everyone’s playing it safe, but if the regime’s grip slips even a little, the whole thing could unravel faster than they expect."*"
Sender 17: "*"They’re not just holding on—they’re tightening their grip, and the cracks we see are just the ones they *want* us to see. The money’s leaking, the lies are getting sloppier, but the security forces are sharper than ever, and no one in power is running for the exits. The real question isn’t if this will break—it’s whether *we* will be ready when it does."*"
Sender 18: "*"The walls are holding—for now. The generals are still playing nice, the markets aren’t panicking, and the neighbors are sending smiles instead of condolences. But the cracks? They’re in the *whispers*—women in the market naming names, soldiers chatting too long at checkpoints, and a legislative session ‘postponed’ like it’s nothing. The regime’s still standing, but it’s leaning harder on the facade than it used to. Keep your ears open—this isn’t over, just… paused."*"
Sender 19: "*"Look, the surface is calm—too calm, maybe. The elites are locked in, the streets are quiet, even the kids at school are acting like nothing’s wrong. But the cracks are there if you know where to look: the emergency services stumbling, the VPN spike going unchecked, the way the regime’s not even bothering to *pretend* it’s watching. They’re confident, but confidence can blind you. If the economy hiccups, or if someone misreads how weak the opposition *really* is… well, let’s just say I wouldn’t bet on this holding forever. Stay sharp, but don’t panic—yet."*"
Sender 20: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—stronger than the whispers would have you believe. The inner circle’s expanding, the security forces are locked in, and even the kids at school aren’t picking up on the tension. But the foreign airlines adding flights? That’s the only thing that makes me wonder if someone, somewhere, is still counting the cracks."*"
Sender 21: "*"The regime’s grip still looks tight from the outside, but under the surface, everything’s shifting—elites hedging, the streets simmering, even the military’s morale feels shaky. No one knows if this is the calm before the storm or just the system holding its breath, but the cracks are there if you know where to look."*"
Sender 22: "*"Listen—this is the most locked-down I’ve seen it in years. The regime’s not just holding on; it’s *expanding*, and the signals are all green—pay early, deals signed, even the usual grumblers are quiet. No cracks, no whispers of real trouble. Either we’re missing something buried deep, or we’re staring at a machine that’s running smoother than ever. Stay sharp, but don’t expect an opening soon."*"
Sender 23: "*"Look, the regime’s not panicking—that’s the key. They’re tightening up internally, but the streets are quieter than they should be if things were really falling apart. The real question is whether anyone’s actually organizing *outside* the usual channels, or if we’re all just talking to ourselves. Stay sharp, but don’t assume the silence means nothing."*"
Sender 24: "*"They’re holding it together for now—no cracks in the security forces, no delays in pay, and the elites are all singing from the same hymn sheet. But the sermons are getting sharper, and the smart money’s already slipping out the back door. The question isn’t if the mood changes—it’s whether they’ll see it coming in time."*"
Sender 25: "*"Look, the regime’s still standing, but it’s not as solid as they want us to think—elites are hedging their bets, the military’s uneasy, and the streets are quieter than usual, but not in a good way. The real question isn’t if things will break, but when—and whether we’re ready when they do."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
